failure_summary.description: The agent added a modifier copied from the passages to a generic answer. 'speech balloon' was given where the key is the bare 'balloon', and 'NFL football' where the key is the sport name 'Football'. The existing 'plain common noun, no added modifiers' rule is worded only for 'one of these / this <generic noun>' clues. It was not triggered by 'Term for ...' definition clues or by 'this sport', so the agent did not apply it.

patch.reasoning: Both failures have the same cause. The agent found the right head noun (balloon, football) and then added a passage-derived qualifier (speech, NFL). The skill already says modifiers like 'speech' are wrong, but only under a narrow trigger ('one of these' / 'this <generic noun>'). The edit widens that one bullet in place, so the skill does not grow. It adds two triggers, definition clues ('term for ...') and 'this sport/game', and it names league, organization, country and sponsor prefixes as droppable. It also adds a bare-word test whose tie-breaker defers to the head-noun exception, so standard compounds like 'Charley horse' and 'hydrogen bomb' stay safe. Rule 3 verbatim archive answers are untouched.

edits.target: - When the clue says only 'one of these' / 'this <generic noun>' and the answer is a common noun, give the plain common noun with no added modifiers: 'a back shaped like one of these' -> 'Balloon' (not 'hot air balloon'). Modifiers copied from passages (hot air, synthetic, funeral, speech) are usually wrong unless part of the standard proper name.
edits.content: - BARE-HEAD TEST (applies to 'one of these' / 'this <generic noun>' clues, to definition clues such as 'Term/Word/Name for the ...', and to 'this sport / game / instrument'): when the answer is a common noun or a sport, give the plain head word with no modifiers. 'a back shaped like one of these' -> 'Balloon' (not 'hot air balloon'); 'term for the circle holding a cartoon character's words' -> 'balloon' (not 'speech balloon'); 'the ball used in this sport is oval, about 11 inches long' -> 'Football' (not 'NFL football' or 'American football'). Drop modifiers copied from passages: kind words (hot air, synthetic, funeral, speech) and league, organization, country or sponsor prefixes (NFL, American, Olympic). Ask: would a trivia key accept the bare head word alone? If yes, answer with it. Keep a modifier only when the bare word alone would be wrong (see the head-noun exception below: 'Charley horse', 'hydrogen bomb') or when it is part of the standard proper name.
